_: Plain-weave cotton shirting / sheeting, ~120-130 g/m2, bleached, no finish; conditioned 20 C 65 % RH. The KES set is one measured fabric (PAL24 control). Jersey knit (T-shirt) differs: much lower B and G, EMT 20-60 %, see `variants_note`. Warp = the stiffer, less extensible direction here.
variants_note: jersey (single knit, 140-180 g/m2): B ~0.005-0.05 gf cm2/cm and G 0.3-1.2 gf/(cm deg) (a cotton-knit patent range and a single-jersey KES study, both via search, E); bending lengths ~1 cm; stretch soft (EMT tens of %). Treat as its own profile when a garment needs it.

alpha.src: no measured BRDF fit retrieved; matte staple-fibre surface with fuzz; Irawan & Marschner 2012 / Sadeghi 2013 microcylinder models are the method to fit it

n.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 mean of 1.578 / 1.532 (recalled)

sheen.v: weak, broad; slightly anisotropic along the yarns
sheen.src: staple fibres and hairiness scatter the fibre highlight

fibre_n.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 cotton n_parallel 1.578, n_perp 1.532 (recalled; inside the brief's 1.53-1.58)

albedo.src: white cotton cloth; not measured here

translucency.v: thin shirting transmits ~10-30 % diffuse light dry; more when wet
translucency.src: no measurement retrieved; the wet rise follows LEKNER88 / ZHANG06

wet_darkening.src: LEKNER88 / Angstrom film model, diffuse light; the index-matching effect inside the yarn (ZHANG06) darkens further and is not in this formula; white thin fabric also turns translucent (fibre/water index ratio ~1.16 instead of ~1.55 in air)

static.src: fabric-on-fabric ASTM D1894 studies report 0.2-0.6, static above kinetic (search summaries, no cotton-cotton number retrieved); wet higher by capillary adhesion

kinetic.src: kinetic below static in every fabric study found; ratio ~0.85 assumed

kes_MIU.src: PAL24 Table 6 (KES-FB4 against its 10-wire contactor, not fabric-on-fabric)

friction.counterface: fabric-on-fabric (E); MIU against the KES piano-wire probe (M)

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: cellulose; recalled literature range, not retrieved

tack.v: none dry; wet cloth clings to skin by capillary films (the wet friction rise in GERHARDT08)

water_contact_angle_deg.src: scoured cotton cloth wicks a drop in seconds (apparent 0); single-fibre advancing values not retrieved

moisture_regain_pct.src: ASTMD1909 natural cotton 7.0 (mercerized cotton and cotton in blends 8.5); Morton & Hearle measured 7-8 at 65 % RH (research/PROOF_REFERENCES.md 4a). Corrected 11-07 ~23:25 from 8.5 (the mercerized value) after proof T4a

water_absorption.src: of dry mass; cotton water-retention and soaked-cloth typical values, not retrieved here

air_permeability_mm_s.src: PAL24 Table 8: 440.4 ft3/ft2/min (ASTM D737-type, 125 Pa) x 5.08 (UNITS); an open bleached shirting

triboelectric.src: ALPHALAB cotton +5 nC/J (humidity dependent, slightly conductive)

surface_resistivity_ohm_sq.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: order of magnitude: hygroscopic fibres fall ~1 decade per 10 % RH (MORTON08 Rs M^n = K, recalled)

collision_thickness_mm.src: half of T0 0.811 mm at 0.5 gf/cm2 (PAL24 Tables 1, 2, 5; inputs M)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: KES-FB3 secant: (4.903 - 0.049) kPa / (T0 0.811 - Tm 0.623) mm (PAL24 Tables 1, 2, 5; inputs M)

initial_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: secant x LC 0.296: LC < 1 means the pile is soft first then stiffens as fibres pack

compressible_to_fraction.src: Tm / T0 at 50 gf/cm2 (~5 kPa, a firm press or sitting); beyond it the fibres themselves resist (fibre modulus, GPa)

penetration_response.ramp_note: stiffening ramp (LC < 1): IPC log barrier starting at collision_thickness, or a two-slope ramp initial -> secant

contact_damping_ratio.src: (1 - RC 35.61 %) / (4 pi): energy lost per press-release cycle; RC from PAL24 Tables 1, 2, 5

restitution.src: a cloth layer dropped or slapped on a rigid flat does not bounce: energy goes into bending and fibre friction (no measurement found)

response_time_ms.src: a cloth flap / slap reads as a short damped crack; set by the in-plane wave crossing a ~0.3 m panel at the speeds below plus bending

wave_speed_m_s.src: sqrt(stretch_N_m 18026 / mass 0.1262 kg/m2) and sqrt(shear_N_m_rad 56.2 / mass); transverse (flutter) speed is sqrt(tension / mass) and depends on load

min_separation_mm.src: two half-thicknesses: folded layers rest T0 apart at light pressure, Tm under ~5 kPa

fibre_density_kg_m3.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 cotton 1.52-1.54 g/cm3 (recalled)

shear_rigidity_N_m_deg.src: PAL24 Table 4 (KES units; x 0.981 for N/m per deg)

drape_coefficient_pct.src: SANAD16 gives the 30-98 % scale only; a ~125 g/m2 plain shirting with bending length ~1.5 cm sits mid-scale

poisson.src: Penava group measured cotton plain weave (Tehnicki glasnik 11(3) 2017) but the numbers were not retrieved; woven fabrics' ratio varies through the stretch

strength_N_50mm.src: TYPICAL shirting strip strength; not measured here

wet_strength_ratio.src: by definition: wet / dry strength ratio, the conditioned dry strength (20 C, 65 % RH) is the reference

recovery.v: poor: creases stay (RT 19-26 %); wet-ironing sets shape

sim._: Per unit width / area; for a triangle mesh with edge length h, spring k_edge ~ k_membrane (square cells) and XPBD compliance alpha = 1/k. Secant to the KES maximum load: the real curve is soft-then-stiff (toe region), so use these as the stiff branch and ~1/3 of it below 1 % strain unless a curve is fitted

bend_compliance_1_per_Nm.src: 1 / bend (N m per unit width); a dihedral constraint's compliance scales with edge length / area of the hinge

shear_N_m_rad.src: UNITS G x 56.19 from PAL24 (mean G 1.00)

bending_length_cm.src: c = (B / W)^(1/3), B gf cm2/cm, W gf/cm2 (Peirce cantilever relation): the cantilever check a sim should reproduce

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: MORTON08 cotton ~1.3 kJ/kgK (recalled)

effusivity.src: sqrt(0.05 x 156 x 1300) W s^0.5 / m2 K; wet cloth is far higher (water fills the air), the 'cold wet shirt'

deform.fracture.wet_strength_ratio.src: COTTONINC13: cotton is 10-20 % stronger when wet; appendix dry 3.0-5.0, wet 3.3-6.0 gf/den

wet.src: E: recalled from Morton & Hearle 2008 (MORTON08), not re-read: soaked ~150 % water (E); cotton fibre is ~10-20 % STRONGER wet (MORTON08, recalled) while the fibre modulus falls; cloth goes limp and clings (bending drop not measured: KIM85 covers wool/PES only); skin-on-wet-fabric friction doubles (GERHARDT08, pairs file); colour by optics_summary.wet_darkening

PAL24.cite: Pal A, Samanta AK, Kar TR. Impact of fire retardant finish on the mechanical and comfort properties of cotton fabric. Indian J Fibre Text Res 49:408-415 (2024). doi:10.56042/ijftr.v49i4.3017. Control fabric: peroxide-bleached 100 % cotton plain weave, 72 x 50 per inch, 126.2 g/m2, full KES-FB set (Tables 1-6, 8)
PAL24.lic: open access (NIScPR); article licence not checked; numbers used as facts

GERHARDT08.cite: Gerhardt L-C, Strassle V, Lenz A, Spencer ND, Derler S. Influence of epidermal hydration on the friction of human skin against textiles. J R Soc Interface 5(28):1317-1328 (2008). doi:10.1098/rsif.2008.0034. Fabric: medical textile 50 % cotton / 50 % polyester plain weave, no finish; inner forearm, 14.8 N, ~140 mm/s, 23 C 50 % RH; 11 M / 11 F
GERHARDT08.lic: (c) The Royal Society; PMC copy; numbers used as facts, text studied only

ASTMD1909.cite: ASTM D1909-13(2020)e1 Standard tables of commercial moisture regains for textile fibres (cotton 8.5, wool 13.6, silk 11, flax 12, nylon 4.5, polyester 0.4 %); read through a CC BY review table citing it (Bioresour Bioprocess 2020, 10.1186/s40643-020-00339-1 Table 10) and the ASTM catalogue abstracts. Commercial (agreed) regains, close to equilibrium at 65 % RH, 21 C
ASTMD1909.lic: paywalled standard; the numbers are facts

KIM85.cite: Kim S-G. Effect of water on the bending properties of wool, polyester and wool-polyester blended fabrics. Textile Science and Engineering (Korea) 22(3):43-52 (1985). Abstract only: bending rigidity of wool and blends rises slightly with water content; polyester falls; bending hysteresis of wool rises steeply up to wool's maximum regain then levels
KIM85.lic: abstract read; full text not opened; direction of the effect used

LEKNER88.cite: Lekner J, Dorf MC. Why some things are darker when wet. Appl Opt 27(7):1278-1280 (1988): a water film's total internal reflection returns diffuse light to an absorbing surface for another chance of absorption (Angstrom), plus a lower relative index inside
LEKNER88.lic: paywalled journal; author copy; formula used, text studied only

ZHANG06.cite: Zhang H, Voss KJ. Bidirectional reflectance study on dry, wet and submerged particulate layers: effects of pore liquid refractive index and translucent particle concentrations. Appl Opt 45 (2006): index matching lets light go deeper and be absorbed; neither model alone sufficient
ZHANG06.lic: paywalled journal; author copy; studied only

SANAD16.cite: Sanad RA, Cassidy T. Fabric objective measurement and drape. Textile Progress 47(4):317-406 (2016): Cusick drape, 18 cm disc / 30 cm sample gives DC 30-98 % from limp to stiff; specimen 24 cm when DC < 30 %, 36 cm when > 85 %
SANAD16.lic: accepted version, all rights reserved; studied, ranges used as facts

MORTON08.cite: Morton WE, Hearle JWS. Physical Properties of Textile Fibres, 4th ed. Woodhead (2008): fibre densities, refractive indices, moduli, wet/dry strength, electrical resistance. Recalled; not re-opened in this session
MORTON08.lic: copyrighted book; individual numbers as facts; recalled, so marked E

ALPHALAB.cite: AlphaLab Inc. (W. Lee) triboelectric table, charge affinity nC/J at ~22 C, 35 % RH (2009); cotton +5, wool 0 read from secondary copies (blog / Scribd); nylon listed with dry skin at +30
ALPHALAB.lic: (c) AlphaLab, may be reproduced only whole; single numbers used as facts, table not copied

UNITS.cite: Unit conversions done here: 1 gf = 9.80665 mN; KES B gf cm2/cm x 98.07 = uN m per unit width; KES G gf/(cm deg) x 56.19 = N/m per rad; KES-FB1 standard max load 500 gf/cm = 490.3 N/m; 1 oz/yd2 = 33.906 g/m2; 1 momme = 4.306 g/m2; 1 ft3/ft2/min (ASTM D737, 125 Pa) = 5.08 mm/s

TYPICAL.cite: Trade and textbook typical values (fabric weight classes, Martindale rating bands such as EN 14465 upholstery 'heavy domestic' >= 25 000 rubs, fabric emissivity ~0.9, effective fabric conductivity dominated by trapped air 0.03-0.06 W/mK). Used only where no measured value was retrieved; each use says why

COTTONINC13.cite: Textile Fibers (2013), Cotton Incorporated: cotton is 10-20 % stronger when wet (dry 3.0-4.9, wet 3.3-6.7 gf/den in the text); appendix 'Comparison of fiber properties' dry / wet tenacity gf/den: cotton 3.0-5.0 / 3.3-6.0, flax 5.5-6.5 / 6.0-7.8, silk 2.4-5.1 / 2.0-4.3, nylon 2.3-5.0 / 1.8-4.0, spandex 0.5-1.5 / 0.5-1.5 (rows identified by density and regain: the PDF text layer shifts the row labels by one)
COTTONINC13.lic: (c) 2013 Cotton Incorporated, all rights reserved: text STUDY ONLY (P13); a few numbers used as facts
